intro: This growth icon shows a zigzag line climbing to an arrowhead inside a rounded square, pointing up and to the right. It signals that a number has risen: revenue, followers, views or savings. Use it on stat cards, trending lists, investment summaries and anywhere a positive change needs a quick visual cue.
meaning: Up and to the right is the shape of any rising chart, so the arrow reads as improvement in almost every culture that writes left to right. Where a full chart means a report to open, the arrow means one value going up. It differs from an export arrow, which points straight up out of a tray, and from a plain up arrow, which means scroll or move up.
uses: Sales dashboard stat card: sits beside the percentage change in revenue compared with the previous period.
Social app explore tab: labels the trending section listing posts and topics gaining attention right now.
Investment app portfolio: marks holdings that have gained value since purchase, alongside the amount and percentage.
Business plan builder: introduces the growth targets step where founders set goals for users and revenue.
tips: Pair the arrow with the actual change in text, such as +12%, because colour and direction alone fail for screen readers and colour-blind users.
Use a mirrored falling version for drops, so stat cards can show both directions with the same frame and stroke weight.
Avoid green for growth in markets where red means rising prices, such as mainland China, and follow local colour conventions instead.

faq.q: What does the trending up icon mean?
faq.a: It means a value is increasing, or that something is gaining popularity right now. On a stat card it shows a rise in a metric, while in a social or news app it marks the list of topics people are talking about most.

faq.q: Which stock icon shows a price going up?
faq.a: An arrow climbing up and to the right is the standard sign for a rising share price. Show the percentage next to it and use a falling arrow for drops. Many apps add colour, but the direction and the number should carry the meaning on their own.
